title: PCPP from completeness and close acceptance
statement: Let $A$ be a finite alphabet with decidable equality, let $n>0$, and let $V$ be a probabilistically checkable proof system for words in $A^n$. Let $P\subseteq A^n$ be a property and let $r>0$. Suppose every word in $P$ has a proof accepted with probability $1$. Suppose also that for every $\varepsilon\in[0,1]$, every word $w$, and every proof, acceptance probability at least $1-r\varepsilon$ implies that some word in $P$ is within relative Hamming distance $\varepsilon$ of $w$. Then $V$ is a PCPP for $P$ with rate $r$: for each $\varepsilon\in[0,1]$, any word at relative Hamming distance greater than $\varepsilon$ from every word in $P$ is rejected with probability greater than $r\varepsilon$, for every proof.
hypotheses_covered: Equality on the alphabet is decidable
